players.product: inspection & metrology for HBM / 2.5D advanced packaging

quarterly_data.signal: Camtek's analyst and investor presentation (October 14, 2026) set an updated financial target model replacing the previous $750m model (the deck says the model reflects goals/targets and should not be viewed as guidance): ~$1.2B in annual revenue organically in ~3 years (doubling revenue). The bridge from ~$600M (2026F) adds +$380M from inspection & bump metrology systems, +$120M from metrology and +$110M from service & software. At $1.2B the non-GAAP operating margin target is 34-36% (2025 operating margin 30.0%), with R&D at ~10% of sales after ~80% growth in R&D spend from 2024 to 2026F; service and software together grow to 12% of revenue, an installed base of ~4,000 driving $140M.
quarterly_data.figure: ~$1.2B revenue target in ~3 years (replacing $750m model); operating margin 34-36% at $1.2B; service and software 12% of revenue

quarterly_data.signal: Camtek's investor presentation breaks down the over $800M of orders received in 2026: ~80% advanced packaging by application (the rest specialty, photonics and other) and >50% from OSATs by customer type (the rest foundries, IDMs and memory makers). The deck says 60%-70% of Camtek business is in high-end advanced packaging and that its customers include all top 20 semiconductor manufacturers, with manufacturing capacity and supply-chain infrastructure being expanded to support the next level of growth.
quarterly_data.figure: ~80% advanced packaging; >50% OSATs; 60%-70% of business in high-end advanced packaging

quarterly_data.signal: Camtek's technology roadmap (investor presentation): a 10th generation bump-metrology sensor designed to measure bumps below 5 μm in height is expected to launch in 2027; HBM4 and HBM4e are expected to continue using micro-bump interconnect; the deck describes Camtek's 8th and 9th generation as the reference for bump-height metrology on CoWoS and CoWoS-like interposers, and the Hawk (chiplets, HBM and hybrid bonding, defects down to 150 nm) as the bump-height metrology reference for HBM4 and HBM4e. Camtek plans to start selling software products in 2027, developed with Visual Layer, the AI company it acquired in April 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: 10th generation sensor launch expected 2027 (bumps below 5 μm); software product sales from 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Camtek's investor presentation puts its organic growth SAM (metrology, inspection in advanced packaging, inspection in wafer manufacturing) at $2.2B in 2026, rising to $5.8B in 2030E. Its stated path to ~$1.2B: strengthen inspection in 2.5D interposers, HBM and hybrid bonding, expand in specialty wafer fabrication and become a major player in the Si-photonics market; expand into metrology and new process steps; and keep its leadership in 3D bump metrology, where it describes a dominant position in OSATs.
